subject: Shiny for twitter data --- and other examples

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Shiny for twitter data --- and other examples
parts:
I'm new to shiny, ggplot2, and the whole R works and I've been blown away by this family of tools since I came across them a few months ago; I'm struggling to keep pace with so much to learn. Recently, I was collecting tweets for some simple text-mining apps (using shiny), and realized that it took some time in creating graphics like a word cloud. How has the experience of users been and how can the speed be increased? Since I'm not a programmer, my code is most certainly inefficient, but I am learning a lot by looking at the program documentation and code others have used in developing their apps. Is there a database of sorts or listing of different uses of shiny and perhaps,all the code used for those apps?

My first attempt at using twitter data (used in an offline manner) with shiny: http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/06/tweetanalytics-interactively-analyzing.html
A couple of previous experiences with shiny (code is really ugly, so not presented; I can share them with anyone if they needed them):
1. Regarding the recently released medicare charge data - analysis focused on Spokane, where I live: http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/05/medicare-provider-charge-data-how-are.html
2. Regarding different cities that were ranked by Bloomberg Businessweek as the 50 best cities in the US: http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/04/interacting-on-demand-with-2012-best.html

Thanks,
Vivek

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Re: Shiny for twitter data  --- an update
parts:
In my earlier twitter application, I think generating word clouds took relatively more processing time than other analyses. In a more recent shiny server application for retrieving twitter data on the fly, I didn't find much of a lag for most of the analyses. Response time, I am sure would be a function of how many tweets are retrieved, among other factors. I would appreciate any feedback on this application, described at: http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/06/twitter-twitter-on-web-who-is-most.html. This could be used to assess popularity among two people/entities. The code can be cleaned up further, but its out there.

Vivek

messages.subject: Re: Shiny for twitter data  --- an update
parts:
Kinda surprised no-one has responded as it is interesting work

I have not had a chance to look at code yet and am really only interested in sentiment analysis and wordclouds but I
 do have a couple of comments

a) It would be more informative if you could replace all references to entity 1 and 2 with actual character string
b) With the time slider , I would personally prefer stops every 10 or 30 secs rather than 1


c) With the sentiment scores, within each entity is the x axis a time? Also are the sentiment scores rated
to a decimal place. All the examples I got were scored 0. It might be useful to see a range to see how text matches up 
with sentiment score. there was also an error input string 3 is invalid UTF-8 when I ran the app

d) Word clouds . I would prefer to see side by side. Also do the various colors have any meaning?

e) Raw tweets. Just gave error invalid multibyte string at '<ed><a0><bd><ed><b1><8d>'

Thanks for doing this. def plan to use it


andrew clark

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Re: Shiny for twitter data --- an update
parts:
Thanks for the inputs. Revised the application (and code) to reflect a few changes.

a) Replaced references to entity 1 and 2 in tables and graphs with their values

b) Time slider  increases every 30 secs rather than 1 second. 

c) Modified the function to count number of tweets for the output in tab 1 to not be influenced by text encoding problem you refer to (invalid multibyte string...).

d) The errors regarding the input sometimes appear to come up because of the characters used in the tweets and how they're encoded- invalid multibyte string or invalid UTF-8. Added a line of code borrowed from http://lists.hexdump.org/pipermail/twitter-users-hexdump.org/2013-May/000335.html. Hopefully, that'll resolve the issue.

e) Sentiment scores would be integers (they add number of matches of positive words and subtract number of matches of negative words).

f) Application address on glimmer changed (....popularity instead of ...Popsenti) - the earlier one was crashing after a changes in the ui and server file. Just created another folder and it appears to work fine with the same content. Strange.

g) Word cloud presentation: We could go with comparative and commonality word clouds, if those are of interest. I like what's currently on :-)


Vivek
